designs.name: One group (no treatment)
designs.use_when: No treatment is compared: a segregating population tested against an expected ratio, traits correlated across units, or raters scoring the same units.
designs.strength: No allocation to randomize; the analysis is about the units themselves.
designs.tradeoff: No treatment comparison; any grouping must be added as a factor.
designs.analysis_note: one group: goodness of fit (analysis.expected_ratio), correlation (analysis.correlation) or agreement (analysis.agreement)

designs.name: Regression on measured predictors
designs.engine: none (units listed in order; covariates are measured, not randomized)
designs.use_when: Nothing is randomized: the question asks how measured predictors (covariates) relate to or predict the outcome.
designs.strength: Estimates slopes per unit of each predictor, with predictions at chosen values.
designs.tradeoff: Observational: slopes are associations, not causal effects; correlated predictors inflate variance (VIF).
designs.analysis_note: covariates are columns of the sample metadata (analysis.covariates); the model lists one term per covariate

designs.name: Completely randomized design
designs.use_when: Units are homogeneous (e.g., one growth chamber shelf with no gradient); few units.
designs.strength: Simplest analysis, maximum error df.
designs.tradeoff: No control of spatial or batch heterogeneity; rarely the best choice in greenhouses or fields.

designs.name: Randomized complete block design
designs.use_when: All treatments fit in one reasonably homogeneous block (bench, field strip, batch, day).
designs.strength: Simple and interpretable; removes block-to-block variation.
designs.tradeoff: Blocks become heterogeneous when they hold many entries (e.g., >20-30 field plots).

designs.name: Alpha-lattice (resolvable incomplete block) design
designs.constraints: Number of treatments must equal block_size * number_of_blocks_per_rep; reps >= 2.
designs.use_when: Many genotypes (tens to hundreds) so complete blocks would be heterogeneous.
designs.strength: Controls within-replicate field heterogeneity with small incomplete blocks.
designs.tradeoff: Requires mixed-model analysis; block size must divide the number of entries.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = genotype/entry; block = incomplete block within rep. Original model text: y ~ genotype + rep + (1 | rep:block)

designs.name: Split-plot design (whole plots in RCBD)
designs.use_when: One factor is hard to randomize at small scale (irrigation, temperature chamber, tillage) and is applied to whole plots; the other factor (genotype) is randomized within them.
designs.strength: Practical for irrigation x genotype trials; precise subplot and interaction tests.
designs.tradeoff: Whole-plot factor has its own, larger error term and few df; power for it is low unless many blocks.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = main-plot factor, treatment2 = subplot factor; (1 | block:treatment) is the main-plot error. Original model text: y ~ main * sub + block + (1 | block:main)

designs.name: Split plot with a factorial in the subplots
designs.use_when: One factor can only be applied to whole main plots (irrigation, tillage) and two others are crossed within them (genotype x nitrogen).
designs.strength: Tests every interaction among the three factors with the main-plot error for the main-plot factor.
designs.tradeoff: The main-plot factor has few error degrees of freedom; subplot factors and their interactions are tested more precisely.
designs.model: y ~ treatment * treatment2 * treatment3 + block + (1 | block:treatment)
designs.analysis_note: treatment = main-plot factor; treatment2, treatment3 = subplot factors; (1 | block:treatment) is the main-plot error

designs.name: Factorial treatment structure in RCBD
designs.use_when: Interest in interactions (genotype x treatment, treatment x sex) and all combinations can be randomized at the same unit level.
designs.strength: Tests main effects and interactions efficiently.
designs.tradeoff: Number of cells grows multiplicatively; interaction power needs larger n than main effects.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = factor A, treatment2 = factor B. Original model text: y ~ A * B + block

designs.name: Factorial treatment structure, completely randomized
designs.use_when: All combinations of two or more factors randomized to units with no blocks: no stated blocking, or an analysis (Cox model for survival) that cannot fit a fixed effect for small replicate blocks.
designs.strength: Tests main effects and interactions with no block parameters to estimate.
designs.tradeoff: No control of spatial or batch variation; use the blocked factorial when blocks exist.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = factor A, treatment2 = factor B; completely randomized, no block term

designs.name: Augmented block design
designs.use_when: Large number of new entries with seed for only one plot each; replicated checks estimate error and block effects.
designs.strength: Screens many unreplicated lines.
designs.tradeoff: Low precision for new entries; error df comes only from checks.
designs.analysis_note: treatment holds checks and test entries as levels; checks estimate the block effects. Original model text: y ~ check_or_entry + block

designs.name: Partially replicated (p-rep) design
designs.use_when: Early-generation multi-environment trials where only a fraction of lines can be replicated.
designs.strength: More efficient than augmented designs for the same plot count.
designs.tradeoff: Needs spatial or mixed-model analysis; layout generation is non-trivial.
designs.analysis_note: Add a spatial residual (AR1xAR1 or SpATS) where the grid trend remains. Original model text: y ~ (1 | genotype) + spatial terms

designs.name: Repeated-measures / longitudinal design
designs.use_when: The same unit is measured over time (non-destructive phenotyping, body weight).
designs.strength: Uses within-unit correlation; models trajectories.
designs.tradeoff: Needs a correlation structure; destructive sampling over time is NOT repeated measures.

designs.name: Resolvable row-column design
designs.engine: not_implemented (see FielDHub / DiGGer); use make_design('alpha') plus add_field_coordinates() and model row and column
designs.use_when: Gradients may run in either direction (fields, greenhouse benches, chamber shelves) and replicates are contiguous rectangles.
designs.strength: Removes row and column variation within each replicate.
designs.tradeoff: Layout generation needs specialist software; analysis needs a mixed model.
designs.analysis_note: Layout generator: FielDHub::row_column. Original model text: y ~ genotype + rep + (1 | rep:row) + (1 | rep:col)

designs.name: Spatial analysis of a gridded trial (SpATS / AR1xAR1)
designs.engine: analysis only: SpATS::SpATS or asreml/sommer AR1xAR1
designs.use_when: Any field or bench trial laid out on a row x column grid; especially large or low-input trials.
designs.strength: Large precision gains (residual variance -49% for sorghum yield in one study).
designs.tradeoff: Needs coordinates for every plot; model checking required.
designs.analysis_note: Full analysis adds a smooth f(row, col) (SpATS) or AR1xAR1 residual (asreml/sommer); this formula is the row/col random-effect core. Original model text: y ~ genotype + f(row, col) + (1 | row) + (1 | col)

designs.name: Systematic (diagonal) check arrangement for unreplicated entries
designs.engine: not_implemented (see FielDHub::diagonal_arrangement); approximate with make_design('augmented') + add_field_coordinates()
designs.use_when: Hundreds to thousands of unreplicated lines; checks spread evenly over the field to model spatial trend.
designs.strength: Even check coverage supports spatial adjustment.
designs.tradeoff: Checks use plots; entries still unreplicated.
designs.analysis_note: Add a spatial trend model for the diagonal checks. Original model text: y ~ (1|genotype) + check + spatial terms

designs.name: Line-source irrigation gradient
designs.engine: layout by distance from line; analysis with correlated subplots
designs.use_when: Water level is the treatment and is created by a single sprinkler line, so it cannot be randomized.
designs.strength: Many water levels from one line; cheap.
designs.tradeoff: Water level is not randomized; needs a correlation model and careful interpretation.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = genotype, treatment2 = irrigation level (distance from the line). Full model also has side of the line and a Toeplitz correlation along distance. Original model text: y ~ genotype * irrigation * side + (1|block) + (1|block:side) + (1|block:irrigation), Toeplitz along distance

designs.name: Augmented-by-tray design (checks in every tray, guard edges)
designs.use_when: Many genotypes in seedling trays or flats (chamber or greenhouse) with too few seeds or cells for full replication.
designs.strength: Tray effects estimated from repeated checks; entries need not be replicated.
designs.tradeoff: Entries compared with low precision; checks use cells.
designs.analysis_note: block = tray; add cell row/col if needed. Original model text: y ~ check_or_entry + (1 | tray) (+ cell row/col if needed)

designs.name: Between-chamber treatments with replicated chambers or runs
designs.engine: studyforge::make_design('rcbd') with run as block and chamber as unit
designs.use_when: Temperature, CO2, light or photoperiod treatments that are set per chamber.
designs.strength: Separates treatment from chamber identity.
designs.tradeoff: Needs >=2 chambers per level or repeated runs swapping assignments; few df.
designs.analysis_note: block = chamber run, unit = chamber. Original model text: y ~ treatment + (1 | run) + (1 | run:chamber)

designs.name: Drosophila vial lifespan design with rearing-bottle blocks
designs.use_when: Lifespan, fecundity or survival assays in vials.
designs.strength: Each rearing bottle supplies every treatment, so rearing effects are blocked.
designs.tradeoff: Many vials to transfer; vial is the unit for food/drug treatments.
designs.analysis_note: Survival outcome: fit coxme(Surv(age, dead) ~ treatment + (1 | vial) + (1 | bottle)); unit = vial, block = bottle. The formula is the Gaussian fallback for mean lifespan. Original model text: coxme(Surv(age, dead) ~ treatment + (1 | vial) + (1 | bottle))

designs.name: Diallel mating design (Griffing methods 1-4)
designs.engine: cross list: all pairs (+/- reciprocals, selfs); field test in alpha/RCBD
designs.use_when: Estimate general and specific combining ability (GCA/SCA) among a modest number of parents (about 5-12).
designs.strength: Every parent combination; separates additive (GCA) and non-additive (SCA) effects.
designs.tradeoff: Crosses grow as p(p-1)/2; reciprocals double it; usually limited to fixed parents.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = parent i, treatment2 = parent j; the two random terms approximate GCA and the interaction SCA (a multi-membership GCA model needs sommer/asreml). Original model text: y ~ GCA_i + GCA_j + SCA_ij + env + rep(env)

designs.name: North Carolina designs (NC I, NC II)
designs.engine: cross list + hierarchical (NC I) or factorial males x females (NC II)
designs.use_when: Estimate additive and dominance variance with more parents than a diallel allows; NC II for heterotic groups (males x females).
designs.strength: Scales to many parents; NC II gives GCA for both sexes/groups.
designs.tradeoff: Needs controlled pollination; many crosses to test across environments.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = male, treatment2 = female (NC I: female nested in male, NC II: crossed). Original model text: y ~ (1|male) + (1|female) + (1|male:female) + env

designs.name: Biparental / multiparental mapping population (F2, RIL, NAM, MAGIC)
designs.engine: population plan + field design (alpha) for phenotyping
designs.use_when: QTL mapping or combined linkage-association mapping.
designs.strength: Known pedigree; NAM combines linkage power with association resolution.
designs.tradeoff: Years of selfing; segregation distortion and residual heterozygosity.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = line, treatment2 = family; the QTL scan is a separate step on line BLUPs. Original model text: y ~ family + QTL + (1|line) + design terms

designs.name: Multi-environment trial with factor-analytic GxE model
designs.engine: make_design('alpha') per environment + mixed model FA(k)
designs.use_when: Same entries in several locations/years; interest in stability and GxE.
designs.strength: Models environment-specific variances and genetic correlations.
designs.tradeoff: Needs enough environments (>= 5-6) for FA structures; complex fitting.
designs.analysis_note: Full model uses a factor-analytic FA(k) genotype-by-environment covariance (asreml/sommer). Original model text: y ~ env + (1|env:rep) + FA(env):genotype

designs.name: Controlled-environment screen validated in the field
designs.engine: greenhouse RCBD/alpha + field MET on overlapping and independent genotypes
designs.use_when: A cheap early greenhouse trait is proposed to predict field performance.
designs.strength: Tests transferability directly.
designs.tradeoff: Pot conditions differ from field; small genotype sets give unstable correlations.
designs.analysis_note: env = greenhouse vs field; the question is answered by the correlation of genotype BLUPs between environments. Original model text: cor(BLUP_gh, BLUP_field) with CI; or bivariate mixed model

designs.name: GWAS + expression (eQTL/TWAS/colocalization) on one diversity panel
designs.engine: panel phenotyping (alpha/MET) + RNA-seq of one tissue/time per genotype
designs.use_when: Link trait associations to genes via expression.
designs.strength: Prioritises causal genes; colocalization tests a shared variant.
designs.tradeoff: Expression is tissue/time specific; needs hundreds of genotypes for eQTL power.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = genotype; genotype BLUPs from this model feed the GWAS (y ~ SNP + Q + (1|K)) and eQTL/coloc/TWAS steps. Original model text: GWAS: y ~ SNP + Q + (1|K); eQTL per gene; coloc / TWAS

designs.name: Ribo-seq with matched RNA-seq
designs.engine: crd/rcbd on conditions; split each lysate into footprint and mRNA libraries
designs.use_when: Translation efficiency or translational regulation between conditions.
designs.strength: Separates transcriptional from translational change.
designs.tradeoff: Low input yields, rRNA contamination, arrest artifacts.
designs.analysis_note: treatment = condition, treatment2 = assay (footprint vs mRNA); counts go to xtail / RiboDiff / anota2seq. Original model text: footprints ~ condition * assay (xtail / RiboDiff / anota)

designs.name: Replicated ATAC-seq (with matched RNA-seq)
designs.engine: rcbd with nuclei-prep day as block
designs.use_when: Differential chromatin accessibility or regulatory region discovery.
designs.strength: Maps accessible regions with low input.
designs.tradeoff: Organellar reads in plants; Tn5 bias; needs IDR-reproducible peaks.
designs.analysis_note: block = nuclei-prep day; counts on consensus peaks go to DESeq2/edgeR with the same design. Original model text: counts ~ condition + prep_day (DESeq2/edgeR on consensus peaks)

designs.name: Two-organism functional validation
designs.engine: per organism: rcbd/crd with independent alleles and sibling controls
designs.use_when: Confirm a candidate gene's function in the crop and a model organism (e.g., sorghum + Arabidopsis, or mouse + fly).
designs.strength: Two independent systems make an artefact unlikely.
designs.tradeoff: Orthologs may differ in function; transformation is slow in many crops.
designs.analysis_note: Fit per organism; treatment = allele, unit = line. Original model text: phenotype ~ allele + (1|line) + block, per organism

designs.name: Latin Square Design
designs.constraints: The number of treatments, rows, and columns must be equal, and each treatment occurs once per row and column.
designs.use_when: Use when two perpendicular nuisance gradients affect experimental units.
designs.strength: Controls two blocking gradients with relatively few experimental units.
designs.tradeoff: Requires a square layout and assumes treatment-by-block interactions are negligible.

designs.name: Balanced Incomplete Block Design
designs.constraints: Every block contains fewer treatments than the total, and all treatment pairs must occur together equally often.
designs.use_when: Use when field blocks, cages, chambers, or assay batches cannot accommodate all treatments.
designs.strength: Allows balanced comparisons with smaller and more homogeneous blocks.
designs.tradeoff: Feasible combinations of treatment number, block size, replication, and pairwise concurrence are restricted.
designs.analysis_note: Check BIBD incidence and concurrence feasibility before generating the layout.

designs.name: Strip-Plot or Split-Block Design
designs.constraints: Two treatment factors are randomized independently to intersecting strips within each replicate.
designs.use_when: Use when both factors require large application units, such as irrigation strips crossed with fertilizer strips.
designs.strength: Makes crossed whole-strip treatments operationally feasible.
designs.tradeoff: Main effects have separate whole-strip error strata and may be less precise than the interaction.
designs.model: y ~ treatment * treatment2 + (1 | rep) + (1 | rep:treatment) + (1 | rep:treatment2)
designs.analysis_note: The residual represents intersection-level error, so preserve the two independent strip randomizations.

designs.name: Split-Split-Plot Design
designs.constraints: Three nested treatment factors require whole plots, subplots, and sub-subplots with separate randomization stages.
designs.use_when: Use when three treatments differ in the scale at which they can be applied.
designs.strength: Accommodates treatment factors requiring progressively smaller experimental units.
designs.tradeoff: Requires three error strata and sufficient replication of whole plots.
designs.model: y ~ treatment * treatment2 + (1 | rep) + (1 | rep:treatment) + (1 | rep:treatment:treatment2)
designs.analysis_note: The schema lacks treatments3, so this formula is incomplete and cannot estimate third-factor effects until the schema is extended.

designs.name: Two-Treatment Two-Period AB/BA Crossover Design
designs.constraints: Exactly two treatments and two periods are required, with subjects randomized to AB or BA sequences.
designs.use_when: Use when the same mouse, animal, or culture preparation can receive both reversible interventions.
designs.strength: Each subject acts as its own control, reducing between-subject variability.
designs.tradeoff: Carryover, period effects, and insufficient washout can bias treatment comparisons.
designs.analysis_note: Validate washout and carryover assumptions; the listed generator requires a wrapper or custom sequence allocation for an explicit AB/BA implementation.

designs.name: Youden Square or Incomplete Latin Square Design
designs.constraints: A balanced incomplete arrangement must satisfy the chosen row, column, and treatment concurrence structure.
designs.use_when: Use when two blocking directions matter but a complete Latin square is too large.
designs.strength: Provides row-column blocking with fewer experimental units than a complete Latin square.
designs.tradeoff: Not every combination of treatment number and incomplete-block size is feasible.
designs.analysis_note: Validate treatment concurrence and estimability rather than treating the arrangement as an ordinary complete Latin square.

designs.name: Cluster-Randomized Experimental Design
designs.constraints: Treatments must be assigned independently to clusters such as cages, pens, tanks, chambers, or plots rather than their members.
designs.use_when: Use when an intervention is shared by every organism inside a housing or growing unit.
designs.strength: Matches randomization to the physical scale of treatment delivery.
designs.tradeoff: Within-cluster correlation reduces effective sample size and requires more independent clusters.
designs.analysis_note: The CRD generator can randomize cluster labels but does not implement the cluster-specific layout; power calculations must account for intraclass correlation.

designs.name: Hierarchical Nested Subsampling Design
designs.constraints: Measurements must retain the identity of their parent experimental unit and any intermediate sampling level.
designs.use_when: Use for leaves within plants, plants within pots, flies within vials, or cells within culture wells.
designs.strength: Separates experimental-unit variation from within-unit biological variation.
designs.tradeoff: Subsamples do not provide additional independent treatment replication.
designs.analysis_note: The formula assumes subjects are nested within units; a separate leaf or measurement identifier is needed if additional sampling levels are modeled.

designs.name: Randomized Design with Baseline Covariate Adjustment
designs.constraints: Baseline values must be measured before intervention and linked to the corresponding experimental units.
designs.use_when: Use when pretreatment body weight, initial plant size, or initial assay activity predicts the final response.
designs.strength: Baseline adjustment can improve precision and correct chance initial imbalances.
designs.tradeoff: Requires reliable baseline measurements and assessment of the baseline-response relationship.
designs.analysis_note: covariate = the baseline measurement (analysis.covariates); slope per unit of the covariate

designs.name: Greenhouse Bench-by-Position Latin Square
designs.constraints: Bench and position factors must each have the same number of levels as treatments.
designs.use_when: Use when greenhouse treatment responses may be influenced by bench location and perpendicular position gradients.
designs.strength: Controls two greenhouse positional gradients without requiring a separate replicate for every bench-position combination.
designs.tradeoff: Cannot independently estimate complex bench-by-position interactions.
designs.analysis_note: Map row and col to the two physical nuisance gradients and verify that the treatment layout is a valid Latin square.

designs.name: Repeated-Measures Design Including Baseline
designs.constraints: Each subject must have a stable identifier and an explicitly labeled pretreatment baseline time point.
designs.use_when: Use for plant growth, animal body weight, behavioral activity, or cell viability measured repeatedly.
designs.strength: Uses within-subject information to characterize response trajectories.
designs.tradeoff: Requires assumptions about within-subject covariance and a strategy for missing time points.
designs.analysis_note: This is a longitudinal response model including baseline as a time level, not baseline-adjusted ANCOVA; add appropriate covariance or random-slope structures when needed.

designs.name: Graeco-Latin Square Design
designs.constraints: Two treatment classifications must form orthogonal Latin squares of compatible order.
designs.use_when: Use when two treatment classifications and two nuisance blocking gradients must be accommodated in one square.
designs.strength: Balances two treatment classifications against two blocking gradients.
designs.tradeoff: Has strict combinatorial requirements and limited ability to estimate interactions.

designs.name: Latin Rectangle Design
designs.engine: not_implemented (see FielDHub::row_column; no Latin-rectangle generator in FielDHub)
designs.constraints: The selected dimensions must permit the supported Latin-rectangle arrangement with balanced treatment placement.
designs.use_when: Use when the experiment has a rectangular growing area rather than a square.
designs.strength: Offers structured positional balance without requiring equal field dimensions.
designs.tradeoff: Treatment balance and estimability are more restricted than in a complete Latin square.
designs.analysis_note: Validate the specific Latin-rectangle construction because not every rectangular treatment arrangement has the same balance properties.

designs.name: Resolvable Incomplete Block Design
designs.constraints: Each replicate must contain every treatment exactly once while subdividing that replicate into smaller blocks.
designs.use_when: Use when many genotypes must be evaluated in small locally homogeneous field blocks.
designs.strength: Reduces local environmental noise while preserving complete treatment replication.
designs.tradeoff: Requires treatment and block counts compatible with the chosen resolution.

designs.name: Square Lattice Design
designs.constraints: The number of treatments must be a perfect square with block size equal to its square root.
designs.use_when: Use for moderately large genotype trials where complete blocks are too heterogeneous.
designs.strength: Organizes many genotypes into equal-sized incomplete blocks.
designs.tradeoff: Restricts treatment numbers and typically needs appropriate replication to achieve useful balance.

designs.name: Rectangular Lattice Design
designs.constraints: Treatment counts, block sizes, and replication must satisfy a supported rectangular lattice structure.
designs.use_when: Use in breeding trials whose entry numbers fit rectangular lattice arrangements.
designs.strength: Provides local incomplete-block control for genotype comparisons.
designs.tradeoff: Valid design parameters are more limited than for general incomplete-block designs.

designs.name: Cyclic Incomplete Block Design
designs.constraints: Treatment allocations must follow a valid cyclic incidence structure for the selected parameters.
designs.use_when: Use when a cyclic incomplete-block arrangement provides a convenient balanced or partially balanced layout.
designs.strength: Generates structured treatment allocations using repeated cyclic shifts.
designs.tradeoff: Some treatment and block combinations cannot produce the desired balance.
designs.analysis_note: Include rep only when the generated design has genuine replicate groups; verify connectedness and treatment concurrence.

designs.name: Partially Replicated Design
designs.constraints: Some entries receive multiple independent experimental units while others remain unreplicated.
designs.use_when: Use in early breeding trials with many candidate genotypes and limited land.
designs.strength: Concentrates limited replication on a selected subset of entries.
designs.tradeoff: Unreplicated entries depend heavily on model-based error estimation and spatial adjustment.
designs.analysis_note: The existing input schema cannot specify per-entry replication allocation, so that additional metadata is required.

designs.name: Augmented Randomized Complete Block Design
designs.constraints: Repeated check treatments must be included across blocks while new test entries may be unreplicated.
designs.use_when: Use for preliminary screening of hundreds of breeding lines against common checks.
designs.strength: Accommodates many candidate entries with relatively few plots.
designs.tradeoff: Most new entries have weaker direct precision than replicated checks.
designs.analysis_note: Represent checks as treatment levels in the model and use their repeated observations to estimate block variation.

designs.name: Multi-Environment Genotype Evaluation Design
designs.constraints: Experimental randomization must be performed separately within each environment and its replicate blocks.
designs.use_when: Use when crop genotypes are evaluated across locations, years, or management environments.
designs.strength: Supports estimation of genotype-by-environment interactions and stability.
designs.tradeoff: Environmental heterogeneity and unbalanced missing trials complicate inference.
designs.analysis_note: The requires vocabulary lacks environment counts and labels, so a multi-environment wrapper is required; FA covariance and genotype stability analyses need specialized models.

designs.name: Matched-Pair Randomized Design
designs.constraints: Each matched pair must contain comparable experimental units with treatment randomized within the pair.
designs.use_when: Use for animals, donor cultures, or plants paired by initial size or genotype.
designs.strength: Removes matched-pair variability from treatment comparisons.
designs.tradeoff: Matching can be inefficient if pairing variables poorly predict the outcome.
designs.analysis_note: Assign each matched pair a unique block identifier before randomization.

designs.name: Split-Body or Paired-Site Randomized Design
designs.constraints: Different treatment conditions must be randomized to distinct comparable sites within each subject.
designs.use_when: Use when opposite limbs, matched tissues, or paired culture preparations can receive different treatments.
designs.strength: Controls subject-level variability through within-subject comparisons.
designs.tradeoff: Treatment spillover or systemic responses can violate independence between sites.

designs.name: Litter-Blocked Randomized Design
designs.constraints: Treatments must be randomized within litters when individual offspring are independently treated.
designs.use_when: Use in mouse or livestock studies where litter origin influences development and physiology.
designs.strength: Controls shared maternal and early-life sources of variation.
designs.tradeoff: Treatment comparisons may be limited by litter size and within-litter treatment availability.
designs.analysis_note: Block denotes litter; when an intervention is applied to the dam or entire litter, the litter rather than offspring is the experimental unit.

designs.name: Batch-Blocked Randomized Experimental Design
designs.constraints: Each batch must include the intended treatment comparisons with randomization performed independently within batch.
designs.use_when: Use when cell-culture passages, processing days, or growth-chamber runs introduce batch variation.
designs.strength: Prevents avoidable confounding of treatment with processing batch.
designs.tradeoff: Incomplete or unbalanced batches can reduce treatment comparability.

designs.name: Longitudinal Repeated-Measures Design
designs.constraints: The same identifiable subjects must be observed repeatedly under a defined time schedule.
designs.use_when: Use for repeated plant height, animal weight, hormone concentration, or growth measurements.
designs.strength: Estimates treatment-associated changes and interactions with time.
designs.tradeoff: Subject attrition and residual autocorrelation require careful modeling.
designs.analysis_note: A random intercept does not automatically model AR1 temporal correlation; use an appropriate longitudinal covariance model when required.

designs.name: Cluster-Randomized Longitudinal Design
designs.constraints: Treatment must be assigned at the cluster level while repeated measurements preserve cluster and subject identities.
designs.use_when: Use when cages, pens, or tanks receive treatments and individual animals are measured over time.
designs.strength: Models both shared-cluster variation and repeated subject observations.
designs.tradeoff: Requires sufficient independent clusters and can have complex correlation structures.

designs.name: Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Design
designs.constraints: Clusters must transition from control to intervention according to randomized rollout times without switching back.
designs.use_when: Use when all animal groups or facilities must eventually receive an intervention.
designs.strength: Allows phased intervention delivery while providing contemporaneous comparisons.
designs.tradeoff: Treatment timing can be confounded with secular trends if period effects are inadequately modeled.
designs.analysis_note: The referenced crossover package does not directly implement stepped-wedge randomization; a custom rollout generator and period-adjusted analysis are required.

designs.name: Cluster-Randomized Crossover Design
designs.constraints: Whole clusters must switch interventions across periods according to randomized sequences.
designs.use_when: Use when pens or group-housed animals can receive different treatments in separate periods.
designs.strength: Provides within-cluster comparisons while preserving cluster-level intervention delivery.
designs.tradeoff: Carryover and period effects can be difficult to separate.
designs.analysis_note: Crossover sequences must be assigned to clusters, not individual animals.

designs.name: Williams Balanced Crossover Design
designs.constraints: Treatment sequences must satisfy a Williams construction that balances treatment occurrence and first-order carryover.
designs.use_when: Use when several reversible treatments must be compared repeatedly within subjects.
designs.strength: Balances direct treatment exposure and first-order treatment order effects.
designs.tradeoff: Requires sufficient subjects, periods, and washout to preserve the intended balance.
designs.analysis_note: The formula does not explicitly estimate carryover; analyze carryover separately if scientifically justified.

designs.name: Incomplete-Block Crossover Design
designs.constraints: Each subject receives only a subset of treatments, with the subset allocation and ordering satisfying crossover balance conditions.
designs.use_when: Use when too many treatments exist for each subject to receive every treatment.
designs.strength: Reduces subject burden while preserving structured treatment comparisons.
designs.tradeoff: Incomplete treatment exposure complicates pairwise comparisons and carryover assessment.

designs.name: Latin Square Crossover Design
designs.constraints: Treatment sequences must form an eligible Latin-square-based crossover arrangement.
designs.use_when: Use when subjects receive treatments in multiple periods and period balance is important.
designs.strength: Balances treatment representation across subjects and periods.
designs.tradeoff: Latin-square period balance alone does not guarantee adequate carryover balance.
designs.analysis_note: The function constructs crossover plans based on mutually orthogonal Latin squares and is not a universal generator for all Latin square crossover sizes.

designs.name: Two-Factor Longitudinal Factorial Design
designs.constraints: All planned treatment combinations must be assigned to independent subjects before repeated measurement begins.
designs.use_when: Use for genotype-by-stress experiments measuring growth or physiological responses over time.
designs.strength: Estimates interactions among the two factors and their temporal trajectories.
designs.tradeoff: Three-way interactions require substantial sample size and complete treatment coverage.

designs.name: Factorial Randomized Complete Block Design
designs.constraints: Every block must contain the planned combinations of both treatment factors.
designs.use_when: Use for genotype-by-treatment or fertilizer-by-irrigation experiments with environmental blocking.
designs.strength: Estimates factorial main effects and interactions while controlling block variation.
designs.tradeoff: The required number of plots increases multiplicatively with factor levels.
designs.analysis_note: Configure the generator for blocked factorial randomization rather than interpreting an unblocked factorial allocation as RCBD.

designs.name: Strip-Split-Plot Design
designs.constraints: Two crossed strips must be subdivided by an additional treatment factor that has its own randomization level.
designs.use_when: Use when irrigation and fertilizer strips intersect and a third treatment is applied within intersections.
designs.strength: Accommodates three factors with different operational application scales.
designs.tradeoff: Multiple randomization strata complicate precision and error-term selection.
designs.model: y ~ treatment * treatment2 + (1 | rep) + (1 | rep:treatment) + (1 | rep:treatment2)
designs.analysis_note: The generic schema lacks the third factor and the referenced generator constructs only the two-factor strip plot; a custom split-stage generator and full analysis model are necessary.

designs.name: Two-Level Fractional Factorial Design
designs.constraints: The number of factors, runs, and generators must define a valid fractional factorial with a chosen resolution.
designs.use_when: Use to screen several culture-medium components or stress factors with limited experimental runs.
designs.strength: Tests many factors with substantially fewer runs than a complete factorial.
designs.tradeoff: Aliasing confounds selected effects and interactions.
designs.analysis_note: The current schema supports only two named factor columns; additional factors and the alias structure must be represented before this can support genuine high-dimensional screening.

designs.name: Plackett-Burman Screening Design
designs.constraints: Factors are normally studied at two levels using a compatible screening run count.
designs.use_when: Use for screening many media ingredients, fermentation conditions, or laboratory processing factors.
designs.strength: Estimates many main effects with a small number of runs.
designs.tradeoff: Main effects can be confounded with interactions.
designs.analysis_note: Only two factor variables are available in the generic schema, so additional factor columns are required to represent a standard multi-factor Plackett-Burman design.

designs.name: Central Composite Response Surface Design
designs.constraints: Continuous treatment factors must have defined ranges, center points, and suitable axial settings.
designs.use_when: Use to optimize temperature, pH, nutrient concentration, or incubation conditions.
designs.strength: Supports estimation of curvature and a second-order response surface.
designs.tradeoff: Axial settings may require operating conditions beyond the original factorial ranges.
designs.model: y ~ treatment + treatment2 + I(treatment^2) + I(treatment2^2) + treatment:treatment2
designs.analysis_note: Treatment variables must be numeric and the layout generator also needs center-point and axial-distance settings not represented in requires.

designs.name: Box-Behnken Response Surface Design
designs.constraints: A standard Box-Behnken design requires at least three quantitative factors with suitable coded levels.
designs.use_when: Use to optimize multi-factor culture, enzyme, or fermentation conditions without testing every extreme combination.
designs.strength: Supports quadratic response-surface estimation with fewer extreme experimental settings.
designs.tradeoff: Cannot be represented completely using only two treatment-factor columns.
designs.model: y ~ treatment + treatment2 + I(treatment^2) + I(treatment2^2) + treatment:treatment2
designs.analysis_note: This formula is only a two-factor projection; add at least a third quantitative factor before generating or analyzing a genuine Box-Behnken design.

designs.name: D-Optimal Experimental Design
designs.constraints: A candidate design space and an estimable target model must be defined before optimization.
designs.use_when: Use when candidate treatment combinations are irregular or conventional factorial layouts are impractical.
designs.strength: Selects runs to maximize information for a prespecified regression model.
designs.tradeoff: Performance depends strongly on the candidate set and assumed model.
designs.analysis_note: The model supplied to optFederov and the candidate design matrix must be constructed separately.

designs.name: Orthogonal Array Experimental Design
designs.constraints: The factor levels and requested run count must be compatible with an available orthogonal array.
designs.use_when: Use for efficient multifactor screening of culture conditions or laboratory workflows.
designs.strength: Maintains balanced representation of selected factor combinations.
designs.tradeoff: Only interactions supported by the selected array are independently estimable.
designs.analysis_note: The schema must be extended to store additional factors and the orthogonal-array column assignment.

designs.name: Microplate Row-Column Randomized Design
designs.constraints: Treatments must be allocated to wells while balancing row, column, and plate-level nuisance effects.
designs.use_when: Use for 96-well or 384-well viability, enzyme, and high-throughput screening assays.
designs.strength: Reduces systematic confounding from plate position and dispensing gradients.
designs.tradeoff: Edge effects and spatial dependence may persist despite balanced allocation.
designs.analysis_note: The field row-column generator requires an adapter to respect plate geometry, reserved wells, controls, and multiple plates.

designs.name: Balanced Sequencing-Batch Assignment Design
designs.constraints: Samples from all intended treatment groups must be distributed across sequencing or library-preparation batches.
designs.use_when: Use for RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, methylome, or other sequencing experiments where processing batches may introduce bias.
designs.strength: Prevents treatment effects from being completely confounded with processing batch.
designs.tradeoff: Batch balancing cannot eliminate all technical variation or correct a fully confounded study.
designs.analysis_note: This formula is a simplified continuous-outcome model; RNA-seq count analysis generally needs an appropriate count model such as a DESeq2 design including batch.

designs.name: Paired-Donor Cell Culture Design
designs.constraints: Each donor must contribute comparable independent culture preparations randomized across treatments.
designs.use_when: Use for primary cells or organoids obtained from multiple donors.
designs.strength: Accounts for donor-to-donor heterogeneity while estimating treatment effects.
designs.tradeoff: Limited donor numbers can constrain biological generalization.
designs.analysis_note: Donor is the subject identifier, and technical wells or repeated measurements must not be counted as additional independent donors.

designs.name: Split-Batch Technical Processing Design
designs.constraints: Biological samples must be divided into aliquots and their processing assignments randomized across technical batches.
designs.use_when: Use when testing library-preparation protocols or sequencing platforms using aliquots of the same biological samples.
designs.strength: Separates biological sample variability from technical processing differences.
designs.tradeoff: Aliquots are correlated and cannot be treated as independent biological replicates.
designs.analysis_note: Define subject as biological sample and block as processing batch; add an appropriate mean-variance model for sequencing counts.

designs.name: Randomized Dose-Response Design
designs.constraints: Treatment levels must represent prespecified doses with independent randomized experimental units.
designs.use_when: Use for drug response, pesticide toxicity, fertilizer concentration, or salt-gradient studies.
designs.strength: Estimates changes in biological response across controlled exposure levels.
designs.tradeoff: A linear model may not describe thresholds, saturation, or toxicity curves.
designs.analysis_note: Store doses numerically for regression or as categories for separate comparisons; nonlinear EC50 and LD50 estimation requires specialized models.

designs.name: Chamber-Clustered Randomized Design
designs.constraints: Treatments applied to entire chambers must be replicated across independent chambers or independent chamber runs.
designs.use_when: Use for temperature, light, or atmospheric CO2 treatments applied to whole growth chambers.
designs.strength: Correctly identifies chambers as experimental units for chamber-level treatments.
designs.tradeoff: Few independent chambers create low treatment-level degrees of freedom.
designs.analysis_note: Plants inside one chamber are subsamples for chamber-level interventions; chamber runs only provide independent replication when treatment assignment and carryover are appropriately controlled.

designs.name: Repeated-Measures Randomized Complete Block Design
designs.constraints: Treatments must be randomized within complete blocks and the same experimental units followed at each scheduled time.
designs.use_when: Use for longitudinal field or greenhouse measurements from blocked treatments.
designs.strength: Combines local blocking with within-unit temporal comparisons.
designs.tradeoff: Repeated observations introduce correlation not addressed by an ordinary RCBD analysis.
designs.analysis_note: Assign globally unique unit identifiers and use an appropriate temporal covariance structure if residual serial correlation is substantial.

designs.name: Multi-Location Augmented Block Design
designs.constraints: Repeated checks must link unreplicated or sparsely replicated test entries across blocks and environments.
designs.use_when: Use for preliminary multi-location breeding evaluations with large candidate populations.
designs.strength: Enables comparison of many unreplicated entries using recurring checks and environmental information.
designs.tradeoff: Treatment estimates can be sensitive to missing checks and model assumptions.
designs.analysis_note: Generate augmented designs independently by environment and assess whether each treatment-by-environment effect is estimable before fitting the full interaction.

designs.name: Nested Factorial Experimental Design
designs.constraints: Levels of the second factor must belong to specific levels of the first factor rather than representing a fully crossed factorial.
designs.use_when: Use when biological strains, culture preparations, or treatment subclasses are unique within higher-level groups.
designs.strength: Represents hierarchical treatment structures without inventing impossible factor combinations.
designs.tradeoff: Nested effects are not interpretable as fully crossed interactions.
designs.analysis_note: The referenced factorial generator requires an adapter to create genuine nested rather than fully crossed combinations.

designs.name: Blocked Crossover Design
designs.constraints: Treatment sequences must be randomized within defined subject blocks while retaining crossover period balance.
designs.use_when: Use for crossover experiments where animals differ systematically by litter, sex, or initial physiological status.
designs.strength: Combines within-subject control with blocking of known baseline heterogeneity.
designs.tradeoff: More restrictive sequence allocation can make complete balance difficult.
designs.model: y ~ treatment + period + sequence + (1 | block) + (1 | subject)
designs.analysis_note: Generate crossover sequences first and then perform block-constrained allocation of those sequences to subjects.

model_terms.description: Every model is an R formula lm()/lme4::lmer() can fit as written, using only these generic terms; study_spec.json analysis.terms says what each stands for in a given study. covariate, covariate2, ... are measured numeric predictors (analysis.covariates gives name, column, unit, transform).
